name: そば切り 川名 (Sobakiri Kawana)

claims.text: Menu offers both 十割 (100% buckwheat) and 二八 (20% wheat) noodles from the same kitchen, plus tempura, so wheat is present and cross-contamination is likely. No dedicated gluten-free preparation is documented.
Lunch set and broths use fish dashi and include tempura, anchovy-pepper rice, and duck-broth soba; no documented vegan-safe preparation.

name: 蕎麦酒場 たかま家 (Sobasakaba Takamaya)

claims.text: Soba is made with roughly 20% binder (commonly wheat) and the kitchen also uses soy sauce and fish dashi, so wheat is present in the kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Menu is built around duck, beef, pork, and fish with dashi-based broths; no separate vegan preparation is documented.
Set meals and the dashi-based omelet use traditional Japanese seasonings; soy sauce in Japan is typically wheat-containing, and no gluten-free soy sauce is documented here.
The kitchen centers entirely on egg dishes and uses fish (bonito) and kombu dashi, so animal products are pervasive throughout the menu.
Ingredients are simple and locally sourced: local eggs, Koshihikari rice, Nara vegetables, and domestic bonito and kombu broth.

name: そうめん処 スルスル (Soumen-dokoro Surusuru)

claims.text: The entire menu is wheat sōmen/nyūmen, including a whole-wheat noodle dish, so wheat is central to the kitchen and there is no gluten-free preparation.
Broths are made from sea bream (fish) using a French fish-stock method, so dishes are fish-based and not suitable for vegans or those avoiding dashi/seafood.
The core menu is wheat-wrapped boiled and fried dumplings, so flour is central to the kitchen and cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Pork dumplings are seasoned with traditional Chinese soy sauce (typically wheat-containing) and star anise.
Vegetable-based dumpling fillings such as pickled cabbage and bell pepper are combined with pork, so they are not vegan as served.

name: すき焼きと牛まぶし ももしき (Sukiyaki to Gyumabushi Momoshiki)

claims.text: The signature sukiyaki broth is made with aged soy sauce, which contains wheat, so the core dishes are not safe for those avoiding gluten.
The menu is centered on wagyu beef with meat- and fish-based broths and seasonings; no vegan preparations are documented.
Signature omurice dishes are finished with a sauce made from Igeta soy sauce (Inoue Honten), a traditional wheat-brewed Japanese soy sauce, so the core menu contains wheat/gluten.
All dishes are egg-based omurice over chicken rice; no plant-based options are documented.
Black drip and single-origin coffees are the core offering and are naturally free of gluten and animal products.
